ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a nitrogen-containing polycyclic transition-state structure, with several curved arrows; according to the problem statement, these arrows are not counted in the connectivity. On the right there is an NH2 connected to the central saturated bridgehead carbon, and an independent proton H+ is also drawn nearby. Below the center there is an NH, forming a nitrogen-containing ring with this bridgehead region. Above is a six-membered ring fragment containing alternating double bonds; below is a fused aromatic polycyclic system, similar to a naphthalene-fused structure. Reasoning: After deleting all curved arrows, use the right-side amino nitrogen as the SMILES starting point, written as N. This N is connected to a saturated bridgehead carbon bearing two ring-closure labels, so it starts as NC12. Traverse along the upper six-membered ring to obtain C=CC=CC1, closing to label 1. Then continue into the lower fused aromatic system, using aromatic carbons, represented as c1c(ccc3ccccc13). The final visible NH connects back to the bridgehead and closes label 2 with N2. The separate proton in the figure is appended as an independent fragment .[H+]. Therefore the overall SMILES is NC12C=CC=CC1c1c(ccc3ccccc13)N2.[H+].

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First redraw the molecule as a plain connectivity graph after deleting all curved arrows. Choose the right-side amino nitrogen as the SMILES starting atom, write it as N attached to the saturated bridge atom C bearing two ring closures. Traverse upward through the phenyl/cyclohexadienyl ring to give the C12C=CC=CC1 portion, then continue into the fused lower aromatic system, assigning aromatic c atoms and ring-closure labels through the naphthalene-like fused ring and closing through the visible NH as N2. Finally append the separately drawn proton fragment as .[H+], yielding NC12C=CC=CC1c1c(ccc3ccccc13)N2.[H+].
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中显示一个含氮多环过渡态结构，带有若干弯曲箭头；按题意这些箭头不计入连接关系。右侧有一个与中心饱和桥头碳相连的 NH2，旁边还画有一个独立的质子 H+。中心下方有一个 NH，与该桥头区域形成含氮环。上方是一个含交替双键的六元环片段；下方是一个稠合芳香多环体系，类似萘并稠合结构。
推理：删除所有弯曲箭头后，把右侧氨基氮作为 SMILES 起点，写作 N。该 N 连接到一个带两个环闭合标号的饱和桥头碳，因此开始为 NC12。沿上方六元环遍历，得到 C=CC=CC1，闭合到标号 1。随后继续进入下方稠合芳香体系，使用芳香碳表示为 c1c(ccc3ccccc13)。最后可见的 NH 连接回桥头并用 N2 闭合标号 2。图中单独的质子作为独立片段追加为 .[H+]。因此整体 SMILES 为 NC12C=CC=CC1c1c(ccc3ccccc13)N2.[H+]。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct graph-transcription route: it does not use reaction-arrow interpretation, only converts the visible atom-bond connectivity into a SMILES string and appends the separate proton fragment.
planner_metadata.image_role: From the image, read the skeletal graph: a central saturated carbon bearing H, an upward phenyl ring, a right-side NH2 substituent, and a bond into an NH-containing fused polycyclic aromatic system below/left; also note the isolated proton label H+ at the far right. Treat the curved arrows as annotations to ignore, not as bonds or structural changes.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to know the required output is a SMILES expression for the shown transition-state structure and specifically that arrows must be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use standard SMILES construction rules: encode aromatic fused rings with lowercase aromatic atoms and ring-closure digits, encode the saturated bridge carbon/ring junctions with uppercase C/N and ring numbers, encode the amino substituent as leading N attached to the central ring atom, and represent the separate proton as a disconnected fragment .[H+].
